title: How would you estimate what UK cinemas take at the box office each year?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "What do UK cinemas take at the box office each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Here is a good first one to practise on. Read the question, pause, and have a go at your own estimate first, even a rough one. Then walk through the answer below and compare. Your number does not need to match; your logic is what counts.
body:
The question

What do UK cinemas take at the box office each year?

The approach

People × cinema visits per year × average ticket price.

Say this out loud before you touch any numbers. It lets the interviewer agree with your plan, or nudge you, before you have done any work.

Step by step

  1. People in the UK: 68M
  2. × 1.8 cinema visits per person per year
  3. × £8 average ticket price

That gives about £979M a year.

Does it make sense?

About 120 million tickets a year, or around 2.3 million a week across the country.

This sanity check is the step most people skip, and one of the easiest ways to impress. It shows you care whether the number is right, not just whether the sum works.

Real-world check

The UK population was about 69.3 million at mid-2024 (ONS). This example rounds to 68 million, which is fine: in an interview, any sensible round number is accepted as long as you say it.

Source: ONS: UK population estimates, mid-2024.

Your turn

Try a similar question in the free market sizing drill, which checks your logic step by step.
outro: If your estimate was far off, look for which step made the difference. That is where the learning is, and it is exactly what an interviewer would ask about.
